title: Fibre-component generic points are relative associated points
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a flat morphism of schemes locally of finite type [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. For $t\in S$, let $X_t$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre [def-pc-scheme-fibre], and let $y$ be the generic point [def-sc-generic-point] of an irreducible component [def-weil-irreducible-components] of $X_t$. Then $y$ is an associated point of the fibre structure sheaf $\mathcal O_{X_t}$ [def-sc-associated-points], hence belongs to the relative assassin $\operatorname{Ass}_{X/S}(\mathcal O_X)$, defined as the union over $s\in S$ of the associated points of $\mathcal O_{X_s}$.

proof.text: Put $T=X_t$. Apply [lem-trf-fibre-component-noetherian-affine-chart] to $f,t,C,y$, where $C$ is the component in the hypothesis. Its local-finite-type, component and generic-point hypotheses are supplied by the item. Choose the resulting affine open $U$ containing $y$ and put $A=\mathcal O_T(U)$. Then $T$ is locally Noetherian, $A$ is Noetherian, and the prime $\mathfrak p_y$ corresponding to $y$ under $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ is minimal. This uses no Noetherian hypothesis on $S$.

source.place: Tag 01T6 (lemma-finite-type-noetherian), applied to the fibre over the residue field; Algebra Tag 00ES (lemma-irreducible), closure and minimal-prime description in an affine chart.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-affine-minimal-prime-stalk-annihilator] to $T,U,y$ and this same section ring $A$. Step 1 supplies its affine-neighbourhood, Noetherian-ring and minimal-prime hypotheses. It gives $w\in\mathcal O_{T,y}$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_{T,y}}(w)=\mathfrak m_y$, and its final assertion gives $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_T(\mathcal O_T)$, proving the first conclusion.

source.place: Tag 02OK (lemma-associated-affine-open), forward implication for the structure sheaf, with Algebra Tag 05BV (lemma-ass-minimal-prime-support) applied to the ring as a module over itself.

proof.text: Write $i_s:X_s\to X$ for the first fibre projection and put $x=i_t(y)$. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre], $i_t$ identifies the fibre with $f^{-1}(t)$, so $x$ is the total-space point corresponding to the given fibre point $y$. Step 2 gives $y\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_t}(\mathcal O_{X_t})$. Hence $y$ witnesses $x\in i_t(\operatorname{Ass}_{X_t}(\mathcal O_{X_t}))$, and $t$ witnesses $x\in\bigcup_{s\in S}i_s(\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(\mathcal O_{X_s}))$. This union of fibrewise images is the relative assassin defined in the statement, proving the second conclusion.
